data.bottom_line: The areas with enough snow to ski are also the most likely places to trigger an avalanche. While triggering an avalanche is becoming less likely, isolated pockets of unstable snow could still produce avalanches 1 to 2’ deep near ridgelines, in gullies, and in alpine bowls. Pay attention to areas where the snow feels hollow underfoot, and back off a slope if you see shooting cracks. __________________________________ SPECIAL ANNOUNCEMENTS: Forecast Operations: Daily danger ratings for Turnagain Pass begin Saturday, November 28. Weekly danger ratings for Chugach State Park and Summit Lake also begin on Saturday, November 28. On December 2nd and 3rd, the Northern Aspects Film Festival 2026 will be showing at Bear Tooth Theatrepub for its fifth year, celebrating the people, places, and stories that make skiing in Alaska unlike anywhere else. These showings will benefit the Hatcher Pass Avalanche Center and the Valdez Avalanche Center. Hope to see you there! Motorized Winter Access: Turnagain Pass opens to snowmachines on Wednesday, November 25, the day before Thanksgiving, per the CNF Forest plan and the new over-snow vehicle use map ( OSVU map ). The remaining motorized winter riding areas on the Chugach National Forest open December 1. Happy Thanksgiving from all of us at the Chugach National Forest Avalanche Center! We hope you enjoy the snowy holiday.
